proposed_revision.instruction: Prepare the shower chair for use.
proposed_revision.context: A bath seat with unequal or unlocked leg extensions can rock or collapse when a person sits. The short-leg fault is present in the initial layout; the instruction does not identify it or prescribe supporting the chair before adjusting it.
proposed_revision.goal_boundary: No prescribed target height: accept every common locked hole within the actual documented range. If a patient-specific target is required, put that height in the goal itself, without mentioning the fault or repair steps.

scoring_proposal.full: All four buttons physically out and latched; all four leg settings equal and within supported range; seat within1degree of level; each foot gap between-2mm solver tolerance and+1mm; chair remains on specified floor/work surface; linear speed<0.005m/s and angular speed<0.05rad/s; gripper samples>3cm clear; all these hold continuously3s.
scoring_proposal.partial: 0.5 when all four legs are physically latched at one common supported height but the chair is still held, moving, tilted, or not resting on all four feet. Otherwise0. No artificial quarter credit for making the wrong leg too long.
scoring_proposal.history: Do not zero a run merely for intentionally tilting an unoccupied chair or shortening a leg. Permanent failures only for explicitly justified actual damage/out-of-bounds events; do not invent patient injury when no patient is present.
scoring_proposal.architecture: Single on_step tracker update with dt accumulation; score()/success() are pure cached reads; reset alone clears timers/history. success_hold_s0 if tracker itself enforces3s.

required_checks: Loaded button press actually depresses button and produces mechanical shortening; score reflects final state, no fabricated injury.
One-handed squeeze+lift may legitimately succeed if physically possible; do not force its score0 merely to claim bimanual necessity.
